paper_title: Joint Detection of Fraud and Concept Drift inOnline Conversations with   LLM-Assisted Judgment
caption: A runtime comparison between our ensemble model and various LLM models on the SEconvo dataset
model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates a runtime comparison of various models in a streaming environment. The horizontal axis contains the categorical models being evaluated, ordered from left to right as Our Joint Framework, ChatGPT, DeepSeek, LLaMA, and Claude, featuring slightly tilted text labels without an overarching axis title. The vertical axis measures "Runtime (seconds)" using a linear scale ranging from 0 to 400, with numeric tick labels spaced at regular intervals of 50 and corresponding horizontal dashed gridlines. A legend in the upper left corner categorizes the bars by color, mapping dark green to "Our Joint Framework" and light blue to "LLM Models." Each of the five bars is outlined in black and annotated with its exact runtime value in bold text centered just above the top edge. Moving from left to right, the dark green bar for Our Joint Framework displays a value of 77. The subsequent four light blue bars correspond to the LLM models: ChatGPT with a value of 190, DeepSeek with 365, LLaMA with 172, and Claude with 243. The shortest bar in the chart belongs to Our Joint Framework at 77 seconds, while the tallest bar represents DeepSeek at 365 seconds. The categories are not sorted in a strict numerical or alphabetical order, but the first bar, Our Joint Framework, is visually emphasized through its distinct dark green color in contrast to the uniform light blue used for all other models.
